bibliographic.title: Assessing the research landscape and clinical utility of large language models: a scoping review
bibliographic.authors: Ye-Jean Park, Abhinav Pillai, Jiawen Deng, Eddie Guo, Mehul Gupta, Mike Paget, Christopher Naugler
bibliographic.venue: BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making
bibliographic.citation_apa: Park, Y.-J., Pillai, A., Deng, J., Guo, E., Gupta, M., Paget, M., & Naugler, C. (2024). Assessing the research landscape and clinical utility of large language models: a scoping review. BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making, 24, 72. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12911-024-02459-6

methodology.study_design: scoping review with systematic search and screening
methodology.sample_description: English-language papers on LLMs in medical/clinical applications identified from MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, medRxiv, bioRxiv, and arXiv (January 2023 to June 26, 2023)
methodology.technology_context: Large language models (e.g., ChatGPT, GPT-3, GPT-4) applied in clinical and medical settings

eligibility.decision_rationale: Scoping review on LLMs in clinical settings that synthesizes ethical, legal, logistical, socioeconomic, privacy, bias, and human oversight themes and proposes a standardized evaluation framework; relevant to regulated LLM governance but not focused on conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, observability, audit logs, or conversational control.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial excerpts were provided; full-text sections on governance mechanisms, conversational interfaces, and proposed evaluation framework require verification.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal based on abstract, introduction, and partial methods/results excerpts. Scoping review design is appropriate for mapping the LLM-in-medicine evidence landscape; authors report OCEBM-based quality grading and a documented multi-database search, but full critical appraisal procedures and reflexivity are not visible in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: Findings are coherent with stated objectives and supported by screening of 55 studies, but supplied text does not fully document synthesis methods or detailed governance-operational controls; relevance to conversational governance is indirect though strong for regulated healthcare LLM use.

coding.theme: Governance-related implications and evaluation of LLMs in clinical healthcare
coding.subtheme: Ethical-legal-privacy barriers, human oversight, and standardized clinical utility assessment

synthesis.main_claim: LLMs show promise for compiling patient notes, assisting patient navigation, and supporting clinical decision-making with human oversight, but clinical use is limited by training-data bias, convincing inaccuracies, and ethical, legal, socioeconomic, and privacy concerns, alongside a lack of standardized evaluation methods.
synthesis.contribution: Maps the 2023 medical LLM literature (55 included studies), discusses implementation barriers and facilitators, and proposes a standardized evaluation framework for assessing clinical utility while identifying evidence gaps.
synthesis.limitations: Authors note limitations in evaluating LLMs' effectiveness and feasibility and call for future directions; full methodological limitations are not fully visible in the supplied excerpts.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence for regulated healthcare contexts: human oversight, ethical/legal/privacy risks, bias harms, and evaluation-framework needs; not primary evidence for operational conversational governance controls.

evidence.claim: Published peer-reviewed journal article on LLMs in clinical settings
evidence.excerpt: Park et al. BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making (2024) 24:72 https://doi.org/10.1186/s12911-024-02459-6

evidence.claim: Study is a scoping review with defined search and inclusion counts
evidence.excerpt: We screened 4,036 records from MEDLINE, EMBASE, CINAHL, medRxiv, bioRxiv, and arXiv from January 2023 (inception of the search) to June 26, 2023 for English-language papers and analyzed findings from 55 worldwide studies.

evidence.claim: Objectives include ethical, legal, and implementation governance themes plus evaluation framework
evidence.excerpt: discuss the ethical, legal, logistical, and socioeconomic implications of LLM use in clinical settings

evidence.claim: Proposes standardized evaluation framework for clinical LLM utility
evidence.excerpt: propose a standardized evaluation framework for assessing LLMs' clinical utility

evidence.claim: Human oversight is identified as a condition for clinical decision support
evidence.excerpt: supporting clinical decision-making when combined with human oversight

evidence.claim: Governance-related risks include bias, inaccuracy, and privacy concerns
evidence.excerpt: limited by biases in training data that may harm patients, the generation of inaccurate but convincing information, and ethical, legal, socioeconomic, and privacy concerns

evidence.claim: Evidence quality was assessed using OCEBM recommendations
evidence.excerpt: Quality of evidence was reported based on the Oxford Centre for Evidence-based Medicine recommendations.

evidence.claim: LLMs are deep learning algorithms trained with human feedback
evidence.excerpt: LLMs are deep learning algorithms capable of interpreting and synthesizing vast volumes of textual data. Using a large corpora of unlabelled text combined with reinforcement training from human feedback
63 articles were eligible for full-text screening, of which 8 were excluded given that their topics did not align with the inclusion criteria. 55 articles were ultimately included.

evidence.claim: Authors acknowledge lack of standardized evaluation methods
evidence.excerpt: We also identified a lack of standardized methods for evaluating LLMs' effectiveness and feasibility.
